note: THE ANCHOR CONTRACT (cinatra#2826, epic #2784 S9m) — the drift alarm between the design pin, the executable DOM expectations and the anchors a capture is graded against. `digest` is a sha256 over exactly three inputs: the acceptance manifest's `specCommit` (read from the manifest, never from here — the copy below is a readable mirror), the `domExpectations` recorded below, and the capture requirement anchors recomputed live from scripts/audit/lib/chat-hitl-capture-recorder.mjs. Moving the design pin therefore invalidates the digest by itself, and so does renaming an anchor, adding a host cell, weakening an observation or changing what a capture must observe. The only way back is an explicit re-ratification: re-examine the anchors against the drawing at the new pin and record the new digest by hand. `node scripts/audit/chat-hitl-acceptance-gate.mjs --print-anchor-digest` prints the recomputed value; nothing writes it, because a digest a script refreshes on its own alarms about nothing. The other half of the binding is src/lib/lifecycle/__tests__/anchor-contract-binding.test.ts, which asserts these `domExpectations` deep-equal the executable ones — so the code cannot move without this file, and this file cannot move without the digest. RE-RATIFIED 2026-08-22 (cinatra#2893): the pin moved to the §V addition drawing the ZERO-CHIP SETTLED READING, and the anchors were re-examined against it rather than refreshed. The two DOM expectation halves are UNCHANGED and that is the finding, not an omission — `carriage` names the ONE owner that draws each kind and the root declarations it is ruled by, and `hostParity` names which host draws each kind and how; the addition gives the recommendation card a new FACE for one state, not a new owner, a new root declaration or a new host. The capture requirements are unchanged for the same reason: a zero-chip settled capture is a `recommendation_hold` in the `decided` state, and the decided contract already asks for the state declaration inside the card root and the absence of every per-chip control — which is exactly what the outcome panel draws. The digest moved on the pin alone, which is the alarm working as designed. RE-RATIFIED AGAIN 2026-08-22 (cinatra#2788, S9d): the design pin did NOT move — what moved is the CAPTURE REQUIREMENT for `trigger_schedule_proposal`, and it moved because the card now exists to be graded. The placeholder-era requirement named `[data-action]`, written before any of §VI was drawn, and that selector matches BOTH the proposal's decision floor and the settled chrome's two operations. Re-examined against the drawing at the pin: §VI's decision floor is `Adjust · Confirm` and nothing else — "this floor is the only new drawing in this section" — while `Cancel trigger` and `Release now` are the SETTLED trigger's own controls, which §VI draws on a card that has already been decided ("two quiet right-aligned controls"). So the requirement is now the FLOOR'S OWN UNION — one selector list naming both floor actions: an undecided capture owes at least one control on it, a decided one owes none. It is a union rather than two members because §VI's floor draws different controls in different phases (Adjust · Confirm live, Adjust alone once expired, §7 step 5), and the audit tier reads a multi-member group as "every member present" — true of the chip row, which renders all three unconditionally, and false here. Under the old wording a truthful settled capture of this kind was refused for showing the controls the drawing gives it, and a pending one could have been answered by a control that decides nothing. The two DOM expectation halves are unchanged: the card's owner, its root declarations and its hosts are what S9d's own gate rows record, and none of them moved with this re-examination. RE-RATIFIED AGAIN 2026-08-23 (cinatra#2788, S9d rework): the design pin did NOT move; the CAPTURE REQUIREMENT for `trigger_schedule_proposal` did, and it moved because the PLAN moved and the plan is the authority for this card. PLAN: Agents Lifecycle (A) §7.2 now reads "The option rows are editable as they stand: until you confirm, you change the proposal directly on the card — the rows are never locked behind a separate step. The floor is **Confirm**", and §7.2 step 2 gives the expired reading the same floor ("stays visible, still editable, with **Confirm** to propose again"). So the requirement that was the FLOOR'S UNION of Adjust and Confirm is now the single selector '[data-action="confirm-schedule-proposal"]': one member, the same one in both undecided phases, present while the card is undecided and absent once it is armed. The `adjust-schedule-proposal` control it used to name no longer exists on any phase or any host. Re-examined rather than refreshed: the ARMED card's own control (Save changes) is deliberately NOT a capture requirement, because a decided capture owes the ABSENCE of the decision controls and listing it would refuse every honest armed capture; it is ratified as an ANCHOR in the one-card gate's set for this kind instead. The two DOM expectation halves are UNCHANGED and that is again the finding rather than an omission — `carriage` names the one owner and the root declarations, `hostParity` names which host draws each kind and HOW, and the rework changed neither: `ScheduleProposalCard` is still the sole owner, still emits the same two root declarations, and still reaches run_card and page_gate_region by composition — what changed is WHERE on those two pages it is composed (a step in the left rail, not a card in the gate region), which the one-card gate's new `region` vocabulary records and this file does not. The digest moved on the capture requirement alone, which is the alarm working as designed. RE-RATIFIED 2026-08-24 (cinatra#2928, lifecycle-b W2a): a FIFTH kind, `agent_hitl_screen`, was registered — the agent pausing to ask for input, which this vocabulary had no name for, so every surface told it apart from a review by pattern-matching the shape of the pause. THE DESIGN PIN DID NOT MOVE, and that is the finding rather than an omission: W2a draws nothing and changes no screen. So the new carriage row names the owner the drawing slice will build and the root declaration it will be ruled by, and the new parity row records NO host at all and OWES three to cinatra#2930 — an honest record of a kind with no card, never a claim that one renders. The other four kinds are untouched. The digest moved on the new rows alone. CARRIED ACROSS THE MERGE-FORWARD 2026-08-24 (PR #2939 merging origin/main): both re-examinations above stand as written and neither supersedes the other — they moved DIFFERENT inputs of the same digest, the S9d capture requirement for `trigger_schedule_proposal` and the two new rows for `agent_hitl_screen`, and the design pin did not move on either side. The digest below is therefore RECOMPUTED on the merged tree rather than re-examined a third time: it is the value the three inputs above now hash to together, and any of them moving again is the same alarm it has always been. RE-RATIFIED 2026-08-25 (design#132, lifecycle-b W1): the pin moved to the drawing that makes the schedule ONE FORM in five readings — §VI redrawn, §X–§XII added. THE TWO DOM EXPECTATION HALVES ARE UNCHANGED AND SO ARE THE CAPTURE REQUIREMENTS, and that is the finding rather than an omission. `carriage` names the ONE owner that draws each kind and the root declarations it is ruled by: §VI still gives `trigger_schedule_proposal` a single owner drawing one form, and striking the Trigger configuration summary and the held-steps list from that drawing removes CHROME from the card — not an owner, not a root declaration. `hostParity` names which host draws each kind and HOW, and its authority is §IX — the four-host matrix — which #132 DOES NOT TOUCH: the schedule proposal still reads Yes on the chat thread, the site widget, the run card and the page gate region, exactly the four hosts this file records. §VI adds no host to that matrix and removes none. What its closing sentence does is refuse a SUMMARY reading anywhere — wherever a schedule is read, on this card, on the run's schedule step or in the widget, it is drawn as this form — which constrains HOW a host draws the kind and not WHICH host draws it, so the transcript and composition marks stand as recorded. The capture requirement for `trigger_schedule_proposal` was RE-EXAMINED against §VI's new table of FIVE READINGS and STANDS WORD FOR WORD: the single selector '[data-action="confirm-schedule-proposal"]', present while the card is undecided and absent once it is armed. The table settles both halves in the drawing's own words for the first time, and it settles them for every reading rather than for a phase someone had to generalise from. Confirm is the floor of exactly the two UNDECIDED readings — first shown, and expired — and of no other, so `pending` owes the selector. None of the three ARMED readings draws it: configured and fired-recurring carry Save changes, and fired-one-off carries no floor at all, so `decided` owes its absence. Adjust, which the requirement stopped naming when the S9d rework took the floor from the PLAN, is now absent from the drawing itself — no phase, no host. A drawing catching up to a requirement CONFIRMS it rather than changing it, so nothing moved. The armed readings' own controls are still deliberately NOT capture requirements, and the table is why: Save changes is the floor of two of the three armed readings and not the third, and Cancel schedule is drawn only beside a recurring one, so requiring either would refuse an honest capture of a fired one-off — the same reasoning that kept Save changes out, now with the drawing's own table as its evidence. §X–§XII draw the CONVERSATION around the cards — the bound row acting, the relayed refusal, the conversation that cannot act — and they give no kind a new owner, no new root declaration and no new host, so no carriage row and no parity row moves with them. The digest below therefore moved on the PIN ALONE, which is the alarm working as designed.
